observations: Corrected SNR model Phi(mean(M_i)/std(M_i)) predicts agreement 0.5648 at n=15 (residual 6.5pp, PASS) and 0.7379 at n=20 (residual 17.8pp, FAIL). C1 requires BOTH within 10pp; n=20 fails by 7.8pp margin.

The corrected model improves substantially over the parent frozen model: n=15 residual drops from 50.0pp to 6.5pp (7.7x), n=20 from 44.1pp to 17.8pp (2.5x). margin_std is a better noise scale than within-iteration SE, but not sufficient at n=20.

Under template invariance, ranking agreement equals proportion(margin_i > 0) exactly: 0.4996 at n=15 and 0.5654 at n=20. This empirical statistic is near-exact (residuals 0.02pp and 0.59pp) but is not a predictive model.

The corrected model over-predicts at n=20 because std(M_i) grows faster than mean(M_i) as n increases: margin_std at n=20 (6.23e-4) is 3.8x margin_std at n=15 (1.63e-4), but margin_mean at n=20 (3.97e-4) is 14.9x margin_mean at n=15 (2.66e-5). The std dominates the SNR ratio at n=20, inflating the prediction.
Mechanism classification at n=20 using corrected noise: SNR=0.637 < 3.0 (margin-deficit regime, C2 PASS). However, C2 is gated behind failed C1 and cannot be used for scientific conclusions.

Power-law extrapolation to n=50: |margin| fit R²=0.197 (poor, due to sign crossing between n=10 and n=15); margin_std fit R²=0.867 (reasonable). Predicted agreement at n=50 = 0.575 (PI90 [0.511, 0.774]). C3 passes (predicted <80%) but gated behind failed C1.

Null control: random noise model predicts 49.9% agreement. Corrected model error exceeds null error at both n=15 (0.065 vs 0.0006) and n=20 (0.178 vs 0.060). The corrected model does not outperform the null baseline.
Baseline reproduction: all parent values reproduced within hash-seed variation (canonical agreement n20 0.5654 vs 0.5595, canonical eta2 n20 0.9195 vs 0.9205).

Template invariance persists on truncated-first-20 subsample (verified in parent). Under template invariance, same-type canonical densities are scalar multiples, making rho=1.0 a mathematical consequence rather than evidence for an independent correlated-noise mechanism.

Status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID and outcome=INCONCLUSIVE: the measurement transaction completed validly and the frozen rule was evaluated mechanically. The corrected model partially captures the mechanism (passes at n=15) but fails at n=20. No scientific conclusion about full-DOM extrapolation is supported.

The corrected model (Phi(mean/std)) fails because it conflates two independent sources: (1) the mean margin determining the sign of ranking flips, and (2) the std of margins determining the magnitude of iteration-to-iteration variation. At n=20, std grows faster than mean, inflating the SNR and over-predicting agreement.

The parent's alternative statistic mean(Phi(SNR_i)) was near-exact but near-tautological: under template invariance, within-iteration SE ~1e-5 makes Phi(SNR_i) collapse to indicator(margin_i > 0). The direct indicator proportion(margin_i > 0) achieves near-exact prediction (residuals 0.02pp and 0.59pp) but is not a predictive model for extrapolation.

The power-law fit on |margin| has poor R² (0.197) due to the sign crossing between n=10 (negative) and n=15 (positive). Extrapolation to n=50 inherits this uncertainty. PI90 width 0.263 (from 0.511 to 0.774) reflects this.
Product consequence: C1 fails, so the experiment provides no usable prediction about whether ranking agreement crosses 80% at full DOM. The Docker re-collection question remains OPEN.

What is the correct noise decomposition for the SNR model? margin_std captures iteration-to-iteration variation but over-predicts at n=20. Possible improvements: (a) use median(|M_i|) / std(M_i) to separate sign and magnitude; (b) use a non-linear mapping instead of Phi; (c) decompose margin_std into within-type and between-type components.

The direct indicator statistic proportion(margin_i > 0) matches observed within 1pp at both n=15 and n=20. This is expected under template invariance but cannot be used for extrapolation to n=50 because it does not model the relationship between n and margin distribution.

The margin_std power law (R²=0.867, d=1.643) suggests margin_std grows faster than n^1, while |margin| grows slower than n^1 (b=0.876). This widening gap is why the corrected model over-predicts at larger n. Whether this is a genuine scaling relationship or an artifact of 4 data points is unknown.
